# CIS_CONTROLS_CROSSWALK.md

## Purpose

This file maps the internal operational cybersecurity control library to **CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1**. It is designed for fast professional use in control design, policy writing, audit planning, implementation prioritization, SOC alignment, security architecture review, and executive cyber-risk communication.

This file does **not** copy full CIS Safeguard text. It uses CIS Control anchors, short paraphrased summaries, Implementation Group alignment, and source links. The enforceable requirement remains the internal control statement in `01_Control_Matrices/`.


## Mapping Type Values

| Mapping_Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Primary | The internal control is a primary operational control for the mapped CIS Control outcome. |
| Direct | The internal control directly supports one or more CIS Controls but may require companion controls for full assurance. |
| Supporting | The internal control contributes to the CIS Control outcome as part of a broader control set. |

## CIS Controls v8.1 Reference Used

| CIS Control | Short Paraphrased Summary |
|---|---|
| CIS 1 — Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets | Maintain an accurate inventory and control of enterprise assets, including managed and unmanaged devices that connect to the environment. |
| CIS 2 — Inventory and Control of Software Assets | Maintain an accurate inventory and control of authorized and unauthorized software, applications, services, libraries, and software components. |
| CIS 3 — Data Protection | Identify, classify, handle, protect, retain, and dispose of sensitive data using appropriate safeguards such as encryption, access control, DLP, and secure transfer. |
| CIS 4 — Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software | Establish, maintain, monitor, and correct secure configurations for enterprise assets, operating systems, software, cloud services, and infrastructure. |
| CIS 5 — Account Management | Establish and maintain an inventory and lifecycle process for user, administrator, service, and other accounts. |
| CIS 6 — Access Control Management | Use authorization, least privilege, MFA, access reviews, and access enforcement to ensure users and identities only get appropriate access. |
| CIS 7 — Continuous Vulnerability Management | Continuously identify, prioritize, remediate, and verify vulnerabilities and exposures across assets, software, applications, and services. |
| CIS 8 — Audit Log Management | Collect, manage, protect, review, retain, and use audit logs to detect, investigate, and prove security-relevant activity. |
| CIS 9 — Email and Web Browser Protections | Protect users and systems from web and email threats through secure browser, email, content, attachment, URL, and anti-phishing controls. |
| CIS 10 — Malware Defenses | Prevent, detect, respond to, and recover from malware using anti-malware, EDR, behavior monitoring, hardening, and containment safeguards. |
| CIS 11 — Data Recovery | Establish, protect, test, and maintain recovery capabilities for data, systems, configurations, applications, and business operations. |
| CIS 12 — Network Infrastructure Management | Securely manage, configure, monitor, and maintain network devices, network services, routing, switching, wireless, remote access, and network administration. |
| CIS 13 — Network Monitoring and Defense | Monitor network traffic, detect suspicious activity, operate defensive tools, and respond to network-based attacks and anomalies. |
| CIS 14 — Security Awareness and Skills Training | Provide role-based security awareness and skills training so personnel understand responsibilities, risks, safe behavior, and response expectations. |
| CIS 15 — Service Provider Management | Inventory, assess, contractually govern, monitor, and manage security risk from suppliers, service providers, third parties, and external dependencies. |
| CIS 16 — Application Software Security | Manage secure software development, application design, code, testing, dependencies, APIs, release, and vulnerability remediation. |
| CIS 17 — Incident Response Management | Establish, exercise, execute, communicate, and improve incident response processes, roles, playbooks, evidence handling, and recovery coordination. |
| CIS 18 — Penetration Testing | Validate security posture through authorized penetration testing, vulnerability validation, red-team, purple-team, and remediation verification activities. |

Establish, protect, test, and maintain recovery capabilities for data, systems, configurations, applications, and business operations. Collect, manage, protect, review, retain, and use audit logs to detect, investigate, and prove security-relevant activity. Maintain an accurate inventory and control of enterprise assets, including managed and unmanaged devices that connect to the environment. Use authorization, least privilege, MFA, access reviews, and access enforcement to ensure users and identities only get appropriate access. Monitor network traffic, detect suspicious activity, operate defensive tools, and respond to network-based attacks and anomalies.	Supporting	KMS-KM-006 maps to CIS 3, CIS 11, CIS 8, CIS 1, CIS 6, CIS 13 because the internal control objective addresses asset/software inventory, data protection, secure configuration, account/access management, vulnerability management, logging, malware defense, recovery, network defense, awareness, service-provider management, application security, incident response, or authorized validation outcomes covered by CIS Controls v8.1.	Current evidence for key classification: approved standard/configuration, data inventory or processing record, owner approval, access/export logs, encryption/key evidence, DLP/privacy/retention evidence, review result, exception record if applicable, and remediation proof. Identify, classify, handle, protect, retain, and dispose of sensitive data using appropriate safeguards such as encryption, access control, DLP, and secure transfer. Establish and maintain an inventory and lifecycle process for user, administrator, service, and other accounts. Use authorization, least privilege, MFA, access reviews, and access enforcement to ensure users and identities only get appropriate access. Collect, manage, protect, review, retain, and use audit logs to detect, investigate, and prove security-relevant activity. Monitor network traffic, detect suspicious activity, operate defensive tools, and respond to network-based attacks and anomalies.	Supporting	TPRM-CONTRACT-010 maps to CIS 15, CIS 3, CIS 5, CIS 6, CIS 8, CIS 13 because the internal control objective addresses asset/software inventory, data protection, secure configuration, account/access management, vulnerability management, logging, malware defense, recovery, network defense, awareness, service-provider management, application security, incident response, or authorized validation outcomes covered by CIS Controls v8.1.	Approved supplier record showing MFA clause for supplier access, supporting evidence, risk decision, owner approval, remediation status, exception if any, and review timestamp.	Sample applicable suppliers and verify MFA clause for supplier access is documented, current, approved by the correct owner, mapped to risk tier, supported by evidence, and remediated or formally accepted when gaps exist.	https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/v8-1	Mapped - Requires audit validation before formal attestation

Identify, classify, handle, protect, retain, and dispose of sensitive data using appropriate safeguards such as encryption, access control, DLP, and secure transfer. Establish and maintain an inventory and lifecycle process for user, administrator, service, and other accounts. Use authorization, least privilege, MFA, access reviews, and access enforcement to ensure users and identities only get appropriate access. Maintain an accurate inventory and control of authorized and unauthorized software, applications, services, libraries, and software components. Collect, manage, protect, review, retain, and use audit logs to detect, investigate, and prove security-relevant activity.	Supporting	TPRM-4P-007 maps to CIS 15, CIS 3, CIS 5, CIS 6, CIS 2, CIS 8 because the internal control objective addresses asset/software inventory, data protection, secure configuration, account/access management, vulnerability management, logging, malware defense, recovery, network defense, awareness, service-provider management, application security, incident response, or authorized validation outcomes covered by CIS Controls v8.1.	Approved supplier record showing reseller and distributor risk review, supporting evidence, risk decision, owner approval, remediation status, exception if any, and review timestamp.	Sample applicable suppliers and verify reseller and distributor risk review is documented, current, approved by the correct owner, mapped to risk tier, supported by evidence, and remediated or formally accepted when gaps exist.	https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/v8-1	Mapped - Requires audit validation before formal attestation

Identify, classify, handle, protect, retain, and dispose of sensitive data using appropriate safeguards such as encryption, access control, DLP, and secure transfer. Establish and maintain an inventory and lifecycle process for user, administrator, service, and other accounts. Use authorization, least privilege, MFA, access reviews, and access enforcement to ensure users and identities only get appropriate access. Collect, manage, protect, review, retain, and use audit logs to detect, investigate, and prove security-relevant activity. Monitor network traffic, detect suspicious activity, operate defensive tools, and respond to network-based attacks and anomalies.	Supporting	TPRM-IR-022 maps to CIS 15, CIS 3, CIS 5, CIS 6, CIS 8, CIS 13 because the internal control objective addresses asset/software inventory, data protection, secure configuration, account/access management, vulnerability management, logging, malware defense, recovery, network defense, awareness, service-provider management, application security, incident response, or authorized validation outcomes covered by CIS Controls v8.1.	Approved supplier record showing supplier law enforcement coordination support, supporting evidence, risk decision, owner approval, remediation status, exception if any, and review timestamp.	Sample applicable suppliers and verify supplier law enforcement coordination support is documented, current, approved by the correct owner, mapped to risk tier, supported by evidence, and remediated or formally accepted when gaps exist.	https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/v8-1	Mapped - Requires audit validation before formal attestation

Establish, maintain, monitor, and correct secure configurations for enterprise assets, operating systems, software, cloud services, and infrastructure. Validate security posture through authorized penetration testing, vulnerability validation, red-team, purple-team, and remediation verification activities. Maintain an accurate inventory and control of enterprise assets, including managed and unmanaged devices that connect to the environment. Identify, classify, handle, protect, retain, and dispose of sensitive data using appropriate safeguards such as encryption, access control, DLP, and secure transfer. Prevent, detect, respond to, and recover from malware using anti-malware, EDR, behavior monitoring, hardening, and containment safeguards.	Supporting	VULN-TOOL-025 maps to CIS 7, CIS 4, CIS 18, CIS 1, CIS 3, CIS 10 because the internal control objective addresses asset/software inventory, data protection, secure configuration, account/access management, vulnerability management, logging, malware defense, recovery, network defense, awareness, service-provider management, application security, incident response, or authorized validation outcomes covered by CIS Controls v8.1.	Evidence for Tool Outage Escalation: current requirement, owner assignment, in-scope asset list, scan/advisory output, priority decision, remediation ticket, patch or mitigation proof, rescan/validation result, exception record if any, and SLA status.	Select a risk-based sample of assets, vulnerabilities, exposures, patches, or exceptions and verify that Tool Outage Escalation is current, complete, risk-ranked, owner-assigned, remediated or accepted, evidenced, and reviewed within required timelines.	https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/v8-1	Mapped - Requires audit validation before formal attestation
